mcqs.q: What did the overwhelming majority of Romanian respondents believe about assessing a dog's dangerousness?
o: It should be determined solely by breed/type
It should be assessed individually per dog regardless of breed
Only government experts can determine it
mcqs.e: Respondents overwhelmingly favored individual, breed-neutral assessment of dangerousness.

mcqs.q: What did a significant percentage of respondents reveal about the existing 'dangerous' dog legislation?
o: Unawareness of the legal regime in place
mcqs.e: A significant share were simply unaware of the legal regime governing 'dangerous' breeds.

mcqs.q: The study acknowledged inconsistencies between which two groups' opinions on preventing dog attacks?
mcqs.e: Inconsistencies existed between community members' and experts' views on attack-prevention methods.

mcqs.q: What effect did the digitally altered photo background have on participants' link-clicking behavior?
mcqs.e: Background type did not significantly affect link-clicking (p=.314).

mcqs.q: What did sociability scores predict about participants' link clicking?
o: They predicted clicking only for indoor photos
mcqs.e: Sociability scores did not predict link-clicking behavior.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude should guide shelter marketing decisions?
mcqs.e: The results underscore using empirical data, not assumptions, for marketing decisions.

mcqs.q: Higher owner income and education were associated with what?
mcqs.e: Higher income and education correlated with higher responsible guardianship scores.

mcqs.q: Which owners had the lowest responsible guardianship scores?
o: Owners of both dogs and cats
mcqs.e: Cat-only owners had lower responsible guardianship scores than dog or mixed owners.

mcqs.q: The study concluded the findings would help create educational materials targeting whom?
o: Low-income/low-education people and all cat owners
mcqs.e: Data inform education aimed at low-income/low-education owners and all cat owners.

journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

mcqs.q: Globally, what proportion of human adults is estimated to be sensitized to cats?
mcqs.e: The review cites estimates that up to 10-20% of adults are sensitized to cats.

mcqs.q: The review categorized cat-allergy impact into which three quantifiable outcomes?
o: Avoiding ownership, relinquishment, and return after acquisition
mcqs.e: Outcomes fell into avoiding ownership, relinquishment, and post-acquisition return.

mcqs.q: According to the review, what trend characterizes human allergy to cats over time?
mcqs.e: Human allergies, including to cats, have been increasing alongside rising cat ownership.

mcqs.q: In which area did students at the WisCARES clinic most report improved confidence?
o: Managing/leading cases, including financial conversations with clients
mcqs.e: Students reported improved confidence in case management and leading financial client conversations.

mcqs.q: Which student group most prominently valued the inter-professional/collaborative environment?
o: Both equally, as the top theme
mcqs.e: Inter-professional collaboration was a major theme among pharmacy students more than vet students.

mcqs.q: Insight into diversity appeared most often as what in the study?
o: An expectation more than a realized end-of-day outcome
mcqs.e: Diversity insight was a common expectation but less often noted as an actual outcome.

mcqs.q: How is pentobarbital sodium described for the US and Canada?
o: The drug of choice for companion animal euthanasia
An anesthetic with no euthanasia role
mcqs.e: Pentobarbital sodium is the euthanasia drug of choice for companion animals in both countries.

mcqs.q: How did animal care industries respond to the 2021 pentobarbital shortage?
o: Conserved the drug and used alternative methods/agents
mcqs.e: The shortage forced drug conservation and use of alternative methods and agents.

mcqs.q: The article's main recommendations focus on what?
mcqs.e: Recommendations target managing future pentobarbital shortages.

mcqs.q: What effect did canine-assisted interventions consistently have on human stress markers?
mcqs.e: Across studies, interventions consistently produced positive changes in human stress markers.

mcqs.q: What was the typical effect on the studied canine stress markers?
mcqs.e: Interventions typically did not cause negative effects on canine stress markers.

mcqs.q: What common methodological weakness did the review identify?
o: Sample timing not aligned to when biomarkers peak
mcqs.e: Many studies failed to time sampling to expected biomarker peaks.

mcqs.q: Did the human-animal bond predict improvements in detained juveniles' stress and self-esteem?
o: Only for self-esteem at end of training
mcqs.e: Contrary to hypotheses, the HAB did not predict stress or self-esteem improvements.

mcqs.q: Which association was significant in the cross-lagged panel models?
o: Cross-sectional HAB quality and self-esteem at the four-week point
HAB and stress at end of training
mcqs.e: Only the cross-sectional HAB quality and self-esteem link at T2 was significant.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about prison-based dog training programs?
o: The HAB clearly drives self-esteem gains
More research is needed into the presumed role of the HAB

mcqs.q: For what percentage of respondents was low/no-contact euthanasia a common and/or stressful ethical challenge?
mcqs.e: 22.8% of respondents flagged low/no-contact euthanasia as a stressful ethical challenge.

mcqs.q: What did respondents say about low and no-contact protocols' effect on patients?
o: They may cause or exacerbate fear, anxiety, and distress
mcqs.e: A key theme was that such protocols may cause or worsen patient fear, anxiety, and distress.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend developing?
o: A toolkit of low-contact euthanasia protocols
mcqs.e: They recommend a toolkit of protocols for performing low-contact euthanasia.

mcqs.q: When a blind dog has no severe systemic disease and a predictably good long-term quality of life, what should the veterinarian do?
o: Inform the owner about differences between human and animal visual perception
mcqs.e: The vet should explain how animals' visual perception differs from humans' before any euthanasia decision.

mcqs.q: According to the authors, a diagnosis of blindness in dogs can sometimes lead to what?
mcqs.e: Blindness diagnosis can prompt an inappropriate euthanasia request.

mcqs.q: How many clinical scenarios of veterinarian-owner conflict over euthanizing a blind dog did the authors report?
mcqs.e: The authors describe four scenarios of conflicting views over euthanasia requests.

mcqs.q: Continued exposure to suffering in the animal protection and welfare sector can result in what?
o: Stress, anxiety, burnout, and compassion fatigue
mcqs.e: Ongoing exposure to suffering drives stress, anxiety, burnout, and compassion fatigue.

mcqs.q: Which two key themes emerged from participants' narratives?
mcqs.e: The two themes were feeling unprepared and 'forced strength.'

mcqs.q: What approach did the authors propose to mitigate these challenges?
mcqs.e: Trauma-informed practices were proposed to prevent burnout and build resilience.

mcqs.q: Despite expressing pride in their work, what did the participating enforcement officers consistently report?
o: Resource inadequacies, communication gaps, and a culture of normalized disrespect
mcqs.e: Officers consistently reported inadequate resources, communication gaps, and normalized disrespect.

mcqs.q: Which concept became central to the study?
mcqs.e: The 'medico-legal borderlands' concept became central to the findings.

mcqs.q: What did the authors advocate to promote best practices and improve working conditions?
mcqs.e: They highlighted the potential of relational coordination to promote best practices.
